claims.statement: Allen had been cheated twice over stake money in St. Louis, which made his backers unwilling to accept Murray as stakeholder.
The belt given to Tom Allen was made under the supervision of Wm. Walsh, who had also supervised the belt presented to Mike McCoole.
Tom Allen said Arthur Chambers had seconded him in an earlier fight.
Tom Allen said a gang from Council Bluffs and Cheyenne tried to force him to lose a fight at Omaha, threatening him with revolvers and bowie knives.
Tom Allen said Ned Donnelly's real name was George Bruer, a laborer he had taken from the streets and trained as a boxer.
Tom Allen expressed contempt for a man printed as 'burn' and for his gang, who had made bold threats.
Billy Edwards said that Tom Allen would beat Joe Goss without trouble in a fair fight.
Jem Mace said that Joe Goss would win the fight barring all accidents.
An interview with Tom Allen by a New York Clipper reporter may soon follow.
As a youth Tom Allen learned the trade of gunmaking in England.
Tom Allen served in the Crimean War and won several turn-ups in front of Sevastopol, which convinced him he had the makings of a champion.
After Allen's death, Lord Barrington wore Allen's silk hat, which J. W. Gillespie had fitted him out with.
Tillie Hartgrove, Allen's housekeeper, claimed the silk hat as a keepsake of the old pugilist.
Paddy Nalty, who had worked for Allen for six years, pronounced the hat the genuine Tom Allen relic.
Tom Allen maintained that a thoroughly conditioned 165-pounder had a perfect license to beat a 200-pounder at the London prize ring game.
Prof. Bill Clark, a St. Louis resident, was an intimate of Tom Allen.
For some time after arriving in St. Louis, C. W. Price was Allen's protégé.
Tom Allen gave John Ryan a terrible beating when Ryan would not keep away from his saloon.
Mike McCool, Tom Kelley and Tom Allen used to meet in the Market Street block between Sixth and Seventh streets to congregate and arrange their matches.
Tom Allen was the biggest backer of Charlie Mitchell in St. Louis when Mitchell fought Sullivan at Chantilly, France.
Charlie Mitchell was one of Tom Allen's particular friends.
Tom Allen handled and seconded Ed Smith when Smith fought Peter Jackson in Chicago.
Tom Allen believes a man born in Birmingham can always beat a man not born in Birmingham.
Tom Allen says Corbett jabbed his way to the championship.
Tom Allen says Corbett never struck a blow in his fight with Sullivan that could be decisive.
Tom Allen said he took Alf Greenfield in hand while Greenfield was working on a canal near Birmingham, England, and showed him how to box.
Fred Watkins backed Tom Allen when Allen was the acknowledged champion.
Tom Allen lost money in the Corbett-Sullivan fight because he had misjudged Corbett, thinking him too light and spare.
Pat Smith, brother of Denver Ed Smith, came from Chicago and also put up at Tom Allen's place.
Denver Ed Smith said Tom Allen handled him when Smith beat Goddard in eighteen rounds before the Olympic Club in New Orleans.
Tom Allen and many people believed Denver Ed Smith could eat up and spit out Sharkey, Maher, Corbett or Fitzsimmons.
Mike McCoole died a pauper in New Orleans and was rescued from a pauper's grave by Tom Allen.
Allen was said to have invested some of his ring money in Missouri farms, which he was said still to own.
Allen was a well-known prognosticator of prize fights, and followers of the ring came to him for his opinion before championship battles.
Allen would settle with any man who dared call him the ex-champion (text garbled).
Attorney Simon S. Bass, named as executor in Allen's will, refused to act.
Allen's bar was in the custody of an agent acting for his daughter.
The feud between Allen and rival saloonkeeper Dan Daly lasted until Daly's death, printed as '18%'.
After Daly's death, Allen went to Daly's relatives and offered his services and substantial aid in money.
Tom Allen had for several years wintered the horse at William W. Heapes's farm.
The horse was in the possession of William W. Heapes in St. Louis County.
William W. Heapes would hold the horse until a feed bill of some $17 was settled.
Tillie Hartgrove had been the housekeeper of the late Tom Allen.
Tom Allen left his property to Tillie Hartgrove for her services.
Tillie Hartgrove nursed Tom Allen before his death.
Tom Allen willed Tillie Hartgrove his property, except a nominal sum to each of his two daughters.
The new manager of Champion's Rest had been a bartender under Tom Allen.
Lord Barrington, accused of the McCann murder, was dressed in Tom Allen's old silk hat, a frock coat and a cane when he walked up and down near Bonfils in broad daylight.
Tom Allen was 5 feet 9 inches tall and weighed under 175 pounds.
Tom Allen's will left everything to his daughter Polly Allen Taylor and to a friend, Tillie Hartgrove.
A family story says Tom Allen came into possession of a diamond belt, emblematic of the world championship, but no one can verify it.
Tom Taylor plans to offer Tom Allen's silver cup to the Missouri Historical Society.
Barney Aaron and Owney Gagin were to second Tom Allen in the Rooke fight.
Col. Fred Watkins was a lifelong friend and backer of Tom Allen.
Tom Allen of St. Louis was one of Charley Mitchell's best friends in America, having known him as a boy around Birmingham, England.
Tom Allen and Charley Mitchell often discussed the tactics of various fighters who had met Allen.
Tom Allen gave Charley Mitchell boxing tips, the most valuable being the deceptive left hook, which Mitchell then improved and used.
Billy Madden says Tom Allen should not be credited with inventing the left hook blow.
Tom Allen claimed he had been in active training for only nine days before the fight with Bill Davis.
Edward O'Baldwin, the 'Irish Giant', arrived in St. Louis from Boston, went around with Tom Allen, and dropped in on Mike McCoole and Bill Carroll.
